column7: F3c: RBACHandler.CreateRole's own permission-assignment loop had the same discard-and-log shape as F3a's replaceRolePermissions -- swallowed every AssignPermissionToRole error, always replying 201 regardless. Found live by coverage-batch-5's fuzz burst wiring REST POST /api/v1/roles/ into the operation catalog: a fault on AssignPermissionToRole's own actor-authority resolution produced a successful 201 with "permissions":null -- an oracle (c) fail-closed-authz violation, not just oracle (a). Fixed by making core.CreateRole run the role-row create and every AssignPermissionToRole call inside one storage.WithTransaction, propagating any failure as an error and auditing only after commit; both REST and gRPC now call this single function. Proving test is the fuzz harness itself -- corpus entry c600067cf4d3bb8e is the permanent regression, no KNOWN-OPEN tolerance needed; see docs/findings/2026-09-21-FINDING-role-update-permission-replace-swallows-storage-errors.md
